subject: biology-2
question: A microbe recovered from a hot spring grows best at 80 degrees C. Its cell wall contains no **peptidoglycan**, and its membrane lipids are built on a different chemistry than those of true bacteria. To which group does this microbe most likely belong?

options.text: It is an **archaeon**, a prokaryote whose membrane lipids and cell walls differ from those of bacteria.
It is a Gram negative bacterium, because all hot spring microbes are bacteria.
It is a virus, because only viruses survive such extreme heat.
It is a fungus, because fungi tolerate heat and lack peptidoglycan.

explanation: Archaeal cell walls lack peptidoglycan, and archaeal membranes use ether-linked lipids instead of the ester-linked lipids of bacteria, so this organism fits the Archaea. Gram negative bacteria still make a thin peptidoglycan layer, so B fails. Viruses are not metabolically active cells, and fungi are eukaryotes with cellulose or chitin walls.
